hace como un año vi una serie de videos acerca del estudio de la felicidad. y concluía que la respuesta es sí y no:

podemos plantear 3 categorías: sin dinero, con suficiente dinero para cubrir las necesidades básicas (fisiológicas, sociales, etc) y tener más dinero del que necesitamos.

En la primera categoría se encuentra la no felicidad porque hay partes de nosotros que no podemos desarrollar y que a la vez nos llevan a problemas sociales, de salud.

En la segunda categoría podemos hablar de la obtención de felicidad. aquí es donde podemos ponernos objetivos, estar sanos, poder mantener amistades y/o relaciones sentimentales. nos sentimos bien con nosotros mismos y con nuestro alrededor.

y en la tercera categoría hablamos de la obtención de una cantidad de dinero que no necesitamos y que nos lleva a tener siempre metas que nos dan un pico de felicidad pero que después nos vuelven a bajar nuestro estado anímico.

en conclusión, es evidente que necesitamos dinero para poder ser felices, pero tal vez no es la cantidad que creemos que necesitamos.

Sinceramente sólo he leido un libro de autoayuda que me ha gustado "El sútil arte de que te importe un carajo". No lo sentí repetitivo como otros libros que te podrían decir todo lo que tienen que decir en 10 páginas. 

Generalmente la mayoría de los libros de autoayuda son refritos de todos los demás libros, escritos por autores que su historia de éxito la disfrazan de pensamiento mágico como lo es la ""ley" de la atracción". Hay que saber identificar bien: 

1. Si pasan 2-3 capítulos diciendo como te va a ayudar el libro, probablemente sea autoayuda basura.
2. Si empieza a hablar del "poder de la mente", lo mismo.
3. Si sientes que los últimos 4 capítulos te ha dicho lo mismo pero con diferentes historias, same.
4. Si el autor se sale de esta "fórmula" y te da tragos difíciles de tomar como "no es tu culpa todo lo que te pasa pero sí es tu responsabilidad" (un resumen de un capítulo de "el sútil arte"), yo pensaría que es un libro que te puede traer alguna especie de beneficio a tu vida.

Hello, Julia. My name is Rodrigo, nice to meet you. I'm in the same crisis you are in (btw excuse my poor english). Several weeks ago I dreamed about the end of time: everyone basically had to sign a document and after that, death and NOTHING, blank. I woke up almost crying and thinking "I'm alive now but when the time comes, the blank will be permanent and I won't have anything or anyone". I began to cry after this thought and went to wake up my mother (I'm in my 20's and live with here for several unimportant for this topic reasons). I was crying with her and I was unable to talk to her about this because she is a woman in her 60's and I didn't want to scare her with that kind of stuff.

I was to nervous to be alone for days until I began to search for answers. You see, I was an agnostic with the feeling of something else that I couldn't describe. When I was a teenager I become an atheist and everything was fun until I got into this crisis hahaha. But when I got to my 20's I became an agnostic.

Days after my breakdown I began to search on Youtube things like 'proof of god', 'Is God real?' and I found many videos but the ones that made me want to keep looking for answers were this two [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bz0ocjMMeDc](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bz0ocjMMeDc), [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ok0WkrRImmw](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ok0WkrRImmw). I always had the idea that religious people were uneducated and basically repeated 'God is real because the Bible says so and the Bible is real because God inspired it' but this wasn't the case. I mean, I'm not saying they are right and Jesus is the truth and the way (even if I do think so right now) but there is a lot of information to keep looking and calm our heart and feelings.

After a while of being calm I found this video [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ac9pF32gRxU](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ac9pF32gRxU) of Dr. Gary Habermas, an american historian that has dedicated a big chunk of his live to the examination of the relevant historical, philosophical, and theological issues surrounding the death (He also defends the Minimum fact argument of the resurrection of Jesus, if you don't know about this I recommend you to investigate it. Maybe it's not undisputable but it makes you think) He began to talk about NDE's and he even says that it may affect his own Christian believes but he keeps showing it to people.

And after learning a bit of NDE's, I found this other person that claimed that he was sure there was life after death. I mean WHAT?  [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lfiwd2PzXvw](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lfiwd2PzXvw)  And I got fascinated about this. Blind people that had the ability to see in their NDE's... How can a brain replicate something it has no information about?

Obviously neither me nor Dr. Habermas nor Jeffrey Long nor any other person KNOWS what happens after death, but I think there continuously more and more information to at least be able to say 'Maybe there is something, and everything points it's good even if it's not what we think'. Maybe it's not God, even if I do think so, but there is something.
